summary: Fresh FOC Heat research for the Sep. 21, 2026 FOC window. No current BUY is justified. The strongest candidates are Hammer Head #1, Dungeons & Dragons #1, Iron Man: Racing Towards Doom #1, and Predator vs. Punisher #1, but each has a material evidence gap. Preserve capital rather than forcing a BUY.
orderingWindow: PRH, Lunar Distribution, Comic Previews, and current retailer listings identify Monday, Sep. 21, 2026 as the next FOC date. M&M Comics states weekly FOC preorders are due 7pm Central every Monday, which is 8pm Eastern for an Indiana buyer. Retailer-specific deadlines can be earlier.

books.title: HAMMER HEAD #1
books.creators: Ed Brisson; Damian Couceiro; Dee Cunniffe; Patrick Brosseau
verifiedFacts: Five-issue horror series; $4.99 standard Cover A; Oct. 14, 2026 release; Sep. 21 FOC.
Jules is the sole survivor of a recurring Hammer Head killing spree and is drawn into a ritual while imprisoned.
Multiple covers are solicited, including standard and foil variants.
marketEvidence: No issue-specific completed-sale evidence exists because the issue is unreleased.
Key Collector's pre-release guide for a Hammer Head #1 variant is $1 low / $2 mid / $5 high; this is a guide estimate, not a completed sale.
Creator history is useful context but does not prove a demand/supply imbalance.
books.thesis: Best low-price horror WATCH in the window. The creative package is credible, but there is no demonstrated aftermarket demand. At $4.99 the downside is not sufficiently protected; at $3.99 or less, one standard copy is a defensible speculation, but not a FOC BUY.

books.title: DUNGEONS & DRAGONS #1
books.creators: Jackson Lanzing; Collin Kelly; Ibraim Roberson; Arabson Oliveira
verifiedFacts: 32 pages; $4.99 standard copy; Nov. 4, 2026 release; Sep. 21 FOC.
New ongoing series built around Mordenkainen, Tasha, Volo and a dragon apocalypse in the Forgotten Realms.
A dragon foil variant program is part of the launch.
marketEvidence: Dungeons & Dragons: The Fallbacks #1 has a current ungraded PriceCharting estimate of $5.84 based on completed sales; this does not establish that the new ongoing #1 will appreciate.

The 2024 Saturday Morning Adventures standard #1 has stronger values than some standard D&D issues, while its limited foil has much stronger completed sales; scarcity/format matters more than the D&D name alone.
No completed-sale evidence exists for the unreleased 2026 ongoing #1.
books.thesis: Major IP and strong creators create collector interest, but standard-copy D&D evidence does not establish a new-issue premium. WATCH at $3.99 or less; no foil or ratio speculation.

books.title: IRON MAN: RACING TOWARDS DOOM #1
books.creators: Ethan Sacks; Greg Land; Phil Noto
verifiedFacts: 32 pages; $4.99 standard copy; Oct. 21, 2026 release; Sep. 21 FOC.
Story ties Iron Man to Atlassian Williams F1 drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon, with Doctor Doom as antagonist.
The earlier F1 collaboration was a promotional exclusive sold through the Williams F1 website, with seven exclusive covers released during 2026.
marketEvidence: PriceCharting records completed sales of earlier promotional/exclusive editions at roughly $100-$138 in June-July 2026, plus other promotional editions around $28-$47.
Those high sales are for promotional/exclusive editions, not the new $4.99 mass-market standard copy, so they show attention but not standard-copy scarcity.
Key Collector currently gives the new standard issue a $1 low / $2 mid / $5 high pre-release estimate with no market-trend data; estimates are not completed sales.
books.thesis: Interesting market anomaly, but easy to misread. The $100+ sales are real completed sales, yet they belong to promotional/exclusive editions. The new standard copy lacks a proven scarcity advantage. WATCH below cover; no premium-variant purchase.
unknowns: Actual print run and retailer orders

books.title: PREDATOR VS. PUNISHER #1
books.creators: Frank Tieri; Jesus Saiz; Dustin Weaver; Fabrizio De Tommaso; Alex Maleev; Leinil Yu; Martin Coccolo
verifiedFacts: Four-issue miniseries; $5.99; Nov. 11, 2026 release; Sep. 21 FOC.
First-ever Predator/Punisher crossover according to the solicitation.
Launch has multiple covers plus 1:25 and 1:100 incentives and a foil cover.
marketEvidence: PriceCharting shows completed eBay transactions for preorders of the exact #1 at $5.99 and $8.80 in August; these are preorder transactions, not post-release aftermarket sales.
Multiverse of Heroes identifies Predator vs. Punisher #1 as one of the week's 1:100 books and counts 57 ratio covers across the full Sep. 21 slate.
No post-release standard-copy sales exist because the issue is unreleased.
books.thesis: Strong crossover premise, but the $5.99 entry and extensive variant structure create a high supply/risk hurdle. Preorder transactions above cover are not enough to establish durable aftermarket strength. WATCH only below cover; no ratio speculation.

methodologyNotes: Completed preorder transactions are weaker than post-release aftermarket sales.
Promotional/exclusive editions are not treated as equivalent to later mass-market standard copies.
Pre-release guide estimates are not treated as completed-sale evidence.
Low acquisition price can reduce downside but does not substitute for demand evidence.
